Article Title: 'SP workers' names will be deleted': Akhilesh claims BJP trying to add fake voters to rolls
Article Text:
Akhilesh Yadav alleged attempts to add fake voters to UP's electoral rolls and warned that SP workers' names could be deleted before the 2027 polls

Akhilesh warns SP workers' names could be deleted

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday accused the BJP of attempting to add fake voters to Uttar Pradesh's electoral rolls ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. He alleged that the ruling party was using Form 6 applications to manipulate voter entries and warned that the names of SP workers and Opposition sympathisers could be deleted before polling.Speaking in Lucknow after the publication of the draft electoral roll, Yadav also alleged that the BJP was preparing to create discrepancies between the voter lists available with political parties and those used by presiding officers on polling day."The number should indeed increase, but we will have to be wary of conspiracies," he said, adding that the SP would examine the increase in voter numbers booth-wise.Responding to the Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer's press conference on the draft electoral roll, Yadav alleged that the BJP was attempting to influence the voter list by adding names of people from other states."The first question is that the CM had said 1.27 crore Hindu votes have been deleted. After that, this increase in number has begun. I can claim that the BJP and its underground-unregistered people are now ready.You would find the names of people from Bihar, MP, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh in the voter list," he said.Yadav also alleged that the BJP wanted differences between the electoral rolls distributed to political parties and the lists available with presiding officers at polling booths on election day."Names of sympathisers and workers of Opposition parties, especially the SP, will be deleted. You will find this on the last day. We will have to be careful," he said.In a separate post on X, Yadav accused the BJP and its allies of attempting to add bogus voters through applications under Form 6. He alleged that the exercise involved the categories of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) voters."The BJP and its conspiratorial allies, sensing their imminent defeat in Uttar Pradesh, are launching a special intelligence campaign to add fake votes under the ‘ASDD’ (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) designation," he wrote.Yadav said the SP had put in place a monitoring mechanism to track every new addition to the electoral roll. It would involve booth in-charges, PDA guards, declared and potential candidates, party functionaries, members, supporters and well-wishers.He said the monitoring would extend from individual polling booths to the Election Commission. The party had also asked citizens to keep track of new voter entries in their neighbourhoods."We will demand an accounting of every vote and will not allow any vote to be added if there is even the slightest bit of dishonesty," Yadav said.He warned that the party would collect evidence against officials allegedly involved in irregular additions and file complaints seeking action against them, including dismissal from service and withholding of pension and other benefits.Yadav's remarks came after Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa announced the publication of the draft electoral roll under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027 on Tuesday.The claims and objections period will remain open from November 17 to December 16, allowing voters and other stakeholders to raise concerns over entries in the draft list.The revision comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with the electoral roll likely to remain a key point of political contest between the ruling BJP and the Opposition SP.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav warns that SP workers' names could be deleted before the 2027 polls. Yadav alleges that the ruling party was using Form 6 applications to manipulate voter entries. Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa announced the publication of the draft electoral roll on Tuesday.

Article Title: ‘Criminal contempt’: Calcutta High Court issues show-cause notice to Abhishek Banerjee over remarks against court
Article Text:
File photo: Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee

High Court directs review of Banerjee's security arrangements

NEW DELHI: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday issued a show-cause notice to Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Abhishek Banerjee , holding that his statements and a social media post against the court amounted to “ex facie criminal contempt”.Justice Krishna Rao directed the Diamond Harbour MP to explain within 15 days of the notice being issued why appropriate punishment should not be imposed on him.Passing the order in criminal contempt proceedings initiated by the court, Justice Rao said he had examined the transcript of Banerjee's remarks and his November 7 social media post.“The Facebook post of the alleged contemnor prima facie amounts to interference with the administration of justice,” the judge said.The court held that Banerjee had “committed ex facie criminal contempt of court” and directed that a show-cause notice be issued to him. The matter will be heard next on December 8.In a separate case concerning the security cover provided to the TMC MP, the High Court, led by Justice Rao, directed the West Bengal Home Department and its principal secretary to convene a meeting of the security review committee within two weeks.The committee has been asked to examine and assess matters related to Banerjee's security arrangements.The court's order comes amid another legal issue involving the TMC leader. Banerjee appeared before Kolkata Police on Saturday in connection with a fresh FIR registered at Girish Park Police Station on October 31 over his alleged remarks against the police.After leaving Bhawanipore Police Station, Banerjee said he had “nothing to hide” and maintained that he had responded to police summons in the past and would continue to do so.“I have nothing to hide. In the past too, whenever they have summoned me, I have gone. If they summon me in the future, I will go,” he told reporters.He also said he would not be intimidated by police action, adding: “Use whatever power you have; put all your strength. Put me in jail, strangle me, but this head will not bow before anyone.”Kolkata Police had served Banerjee a notice asking him to appear before the investigating officer on November 20 in connection with the FIR, according to news agency ANI.The complaint concerns alleged remarks made by the TMC MP against the police.
Article Summary: Calcutta High Court issues show-cause notice to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee. Justice Krishna Rao held that Banerji's statements and a social media post against the court amounted to “ex facie criminal contempt” Justice Rao directed the Diamond Harbour MP to explain within 15 days of the notice being issued.

Article Title: No froth along 52-km stretch of Yamuna in Delhi: Water minister Parvesh Sahib Singh
Article Text:
“Seeing that the BJP has won the hearts of Purvanchali people, AAP is pained,” Singh said (Representative image: AP).

NEW DELHI: Delhi water minister Parvesh Sahib Singh claimed on Tuesday that no froth was present anywhere along the 52-km section of the Yamuna that passes through the national capital.Speaking at a press conference, Singh dismissed allegations by the Aam Aadmi Party that devotees had been made to observe Chhath Puja at spots where the river was covered in froth.“Seeing that the BJP has won the hearts of Purvanchali people, AAP is pained,” Singh said, as per PTI.“Chhath was celebrated with a lot of reverence and lakhs of people were so happy with the preparations,” he added.However, Singh noted that the Delhi government was in talks with Uttar Pradesh to tackle the issue in areas near the Okhla Barrage, which lies on the UP-Delhi border.The Okhla Barrage is often highlighted for the recurring formation of toxic froth on the Yamuna's surface.According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), monitoring conducted at Kalindi Kunj, downstream of the Okhla Barrage, between 2022 and 2024 found that the sudden fall of water from the barrage agitates foaming agents present in wastewater, causing foam to form and float on the Yamuna's surface.Surfactants found in detergents are the main foaming agents in untreated or partially treated sewage.Separately, a study titled Study on Yamuna Frothing in Delhi, conducted by the Energy and Resources Institute (Teri) for the Delhi government's environment department, identified poor water quality as the primary trigger for froth formation. It pointed to factors including effluents containing high levels of ammonia and phosphate released from anionic surfactants.
Article Summary: Delhi water minister Parvesh Sahib Singh claimed on Tuesday that no froth was present anywhere along the 52-km section of the Yamuna that passes through the national capital. Singh dismissed allegations by the Aam Aadmi Party that devotees had been made to observe Chhath Puja at spots where the river was covered in froth.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. Article Title: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam to fight Manipur assembly polls
Article Text:
Angomcha Bimol Akoijam

GUWAHATI: Congress Lok Sabha MP from Manipur and JNU professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam has announced that he will contest the state assembly elections, which are due next year.Akoijam said in Imphal on Sunday he had discussed the election strategy with state Congress president and former CM O Ibobi Singh on “how to form a Congress govt and save the land from BJP and its surrogate parties. Following the discussions, it was decided that I would contest from the Keisamthong constituency”.Party insiders said Akoijam’s name is among those being considered for the chief ministerial position as Congress attempts to regain control of govt after a decade.The Inner Manipur MP’s decision comes as he continues to face legal proceedings linked to his dismissal from JNU and allegations of sexual harassment following an internal inquiry.Akoijam (59) a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems in JNU’s School of Social Sciences, was dismissed on Oct 9 following an internal inquiry. The Delhi high court has since stayed the dismissal, while a separate criminal investigation is pending with the Delhi Police.Akoijam has denied the allegations and called the action a “witch hunt”. He has claimed that he was not allowed to respond to the inquiry committee’s findings.The Keisamthong constituency, located in Imphal West district, is currently represented by independent MLA Sapam Nishikant Singh.Akoijam appealed to his supporters to vote for Congress and elect its candidates in all constituencies to give the party a majority.“By being part of the govt, we will have the opportunity to redirect the future of the state by bringing peace among communities and fostering economic development,” he said.Assembly elections in Manipur are due in Feb next year.
Article Summary: Angomcha Bimol Akoijam is a Congress Lok Sabha MP from Manipur. The Inner Manipur MP’s decision comes as he continues to face legal proceedings linked to his dismissal from JNU and allegations of sexual harassment. The Delhi high court has since stayed the dismissal, while a separate criminal investigation is pending.

KANPUR: A 22-year-old son of a paper businessman died after falling from the sixth-floor balcony of Tower-2 at Rudra Green Apartment in Bithoor police station area of the district on Saturday.According to police, Sambhav Khandelwal, son of Kaushalpuri resident Vishal Khandelwal, had gone to meet a friend residing in a flat in the apartment around 3.30 pm.He was taken to a private hospital after the fall, but doctors declared him dead.His family members reached the hospital after being informed. Article Title: Former Jharkhand Congress president inducted into Manipur screening committee

Former Jharkhand Pradesh Congress Committee president Rajesh Thakur was on Monday named a member of the Congress party’s screening committee in Manipur ahead of the state assembly election in the strife-torn state.Thakur, a seasoned politician, will join a three-member panel headed by B M Sandeep and Lok Sabha MP Hibi Eden as a member. His appointment was a part of a broader organisational changes by the All India Congress Committee (AICC) in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur.“The panel will play a key role in evaluating prospective candidates and assisting the party leadership in finalising nominees for the assembly polls,“ Thakur said.Incumbent state Congress president Keshav Mahto Kamlesh and state general secretary Alok Kumar Dubey welcomed the appointment. “His inclusion in the panel will enhance the profile of Jharkhand Congress nationally and boost the morale of party workers statewide,” Kamlesh said.Screening committees, veteran party functionaries said, play a crucial role in the Congress election process by carrying out scrutiny of prospective candidates and providing feedback to the national leadership before distribution of tickets.“It was the first time since Jharkhand’s formation in 2000 that a Congress worker from the state has been entrusted with such an important responsibility in a screening committee constituted for another state’s elections,” said Dubey.
Article Summary: Thakur will join a three-member panel headed by B M Sandeep and Lok Sabha MP Hibi Eden as a member. His appointment was a part of a broader organisational changes by the All India Congress Committee in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur.

Article Title: Man killed, 2 others injured as speeding pickup van hits two-wheeler in Hazaribag

A 32-year-old motorcyclist was killed, and two others were critically injured when a speeding vehicle hit his two-wheeler from the rear under Bara Bazaar police station limits on Tuesday.The deceased, identified as Naushad Alam, was a painter and lived in Banha Nawada (Harhad). He was returning home with his associates, Shahnawaz and Asim, when their two-wheeler was hit near Yashwantnagar Chowk on Markham College Road. Naushad was taken to Sheikh Bhikhari Medical College and Hospital by locals and the police, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.Locals claimed the driver of the vehicle, which belonged to a private company and was coming from Barkagaon, was speeding under the influence of alcohol. He was detained by the police. Locals blocked Hazaribag-Barkagaon Road, leading to a traffic congestion from Shankarpur Chowk to Dhengura that lasted over six hours, demanding compensation for Naushad’s elderly parents, wife and two children.The blockade was lifted after officials agreed to compensate the deceased’s family. T N Choubey, an official of the company’s administrative department, said, “The company provided Rs 10 lakh as compensation to the bereaved family and assured that it would bear the medical expenses of the two injured youths.“ Following the assurance, the protesters withdrew the blockade around 2 pm.“The road was cleared and traffic resumed after the protest was called off,” Mukesh Kumar Rajak, the officer in-charge of Bara Bazaar police station, said.
Article Summary: A 32-year-old motorcyclist was killed, and two others were critically injured when a speeding vehicle hit his two-wheeler from the rear on Tuesday. Locals blocked the Hazaribag-Barkagaon Road for over six hours demanding compensation for Naushad’s family.

Article Title: Deshmukh retains Latur DCC Bank as Congress-backed panel wins 14 of 19 seats, Mahayuti secures just 5 amid rift within alliance
Article Text:
Former Congress MLA Dhiraj Deshmukh during the victory rally on Monday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

Congress-backed Sahakar Panel has decisively retained control of Latur District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank, winning 14of the 19 director seats and handing Mahayuti-backed Parivartan Panel a resounding defeat in one of Marathwada’s most closely watched cooperative battles.Led by former Congress MLA Dhiraj Deshmukh, son of the late chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh , Sahakar Panel secured 10 of the 15 seats contested on Monday. The tally added to four directors who had already been elected unopposed, cementing the panel’s dominance. The campaign was guided by veteran politician Diliprao Deshmukh and bolstered by a cross-party understanding with cooperation minister Babasaheb Patil, a factor widely seen as crucial to the outcome.For Dhiraj Deshmukh, the victory marks a significant political comeback after his defeat in the 2024 assembly elections. “We could reach out to voters with our work done in the past. For every criticism of opposition, we focused on showcasing our performance,” he said.Emphasising that cooperative elections should not be viewed through a purely political lens, Deshmukh said he was willing to work with opposition-backed directors for the welfare of farmers and the development of Latur.The result is a major setback for Mahayuti, which had fielded its top local leadership in a bid to wrest control of the cooperative institution. BJP MLAs Sambhaji Patil Nilangekar, Ramesh Karad and Abhimanyu Pawar, along with NCP MLA Sanjay Bansode, campaigned extensively for Parivartan Panel. The alliance, however, managed to secure just five seats.The lone highlight for Mahayuti came in the Nilanga Society constituency, where BJP state secretary Arvind Patil Nilangekar (brother of Sambhaji Patil Nilangekar) defeated his aunt in a closely watched family contest. Arvind alleged that the rival camp had resorted to unfair tactics, including the rejection of nomination forms of opposition candidates. “Despite the challenges, we have established a foothold in the DCC Bank. Our representation may be small, but it will be sufficient to ensure checks and balances in the bank’s functioning,” he said.The election also exposed fault lines within Mahayuti in Marathwada. Cooperation minister Babasaheb Patil’s decision to align with the Deshmukh camp instead of BJP nominee is believed to have weakened the alliance’s campaign on the ground and contributed significantly to the Congress-backed panel’s victory.The high-stakes contest recorded an impressive 99.4% turnout, with 993 of the 999 eligible voters casting their ballots on Sunday.The outcome assumes added significance as it comes months after the 2024 Maharashtra assembly elections, in which Mahayuti won five of Latur district’s six seats and BJP emerged as the dominant force with victories in Latur Rural, Nilanga and Ausa. The DCC Bank result is likely to be viewed within BJP ranks as a warning sign that the party has yet to translate its assembly poll success into control of key cooperative institutions in the district.
Article Summary: Congress-backed Sahakar Panel has decisively retained control of Latur District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank. The result is a major setback for Mahayuti, which had fielded its top local leadership in a bid to wrest control of the cooperative institution.

Article Title: Mahayuti split takes centre stage as Latur DCC Bank goes to polls today
Article Text:
Latur District Central Cooperative Bank

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

The election to Latur District Central Cooperative Bank on Sunday has emerged as the clearest public sign yet of cracks within Mahayuti.The contest pits Congress-backed Sahakar Panel, led by former MLA and bank chairperson Dhiraj Deshmukh, against Mahayuti-backed Rayateche Raje Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Parivartan Panel, fielded jointly by BJP NCP and Shiv Sena . Dhiraj is the son of former chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh.At the centre of the rift is cooperation minister and NCP member Babasaheb Patil, who broke ranks with the alliance and backed the Congress panel. In Oct, Patil rejected Mahayuti’s plan for a united contest, saying, “I had a 40-year association with the Congress panel. Moreover, cooperative elections are not fought on party symbols.”Patil later attended the nomination filing of Congress-panel candidate Avinash Patil from the Ahmedpur society constituency, making his stand public.BJP responded sharply. Former minister Sambhaji Patil Nilangekar alleged that Patil had aligned with Dhiraj Deshmukh and raised the issue with NCP leadership, seeking action against the minister. The controversy put Mahayuti’s unity under scrutiny, with the state’s cooperation minister openly campaigning against the alliance’s own panel.In an attempt to contain the fallout, Mahayuti members launched Parivartan Panel in Nov.BJP MLC Baswaraj Patil, Nilangekar, MLAs Sanjay Bansode and Ramesh Karad, and former minister Vinayakrao Patil attended the event, accusing the bank of benefiting a particular family instead of farmers.Sahakar Panel has highlighted its performance record, citing annual profits of over Rs 100 crore, crop loans worth Rs 1,780 crore, net profits of Rs 249 crore, recruitment of 263 local youths and 13 awards. It has promised new branches in every taluka, interest-free marriage loans, education loans and full computerisation.Parivartan Panel has challenged several of those claims, particularly on interest-free farmer loans, and positioned itself as an alternative focused on farmers’ interests.The election will determine control of a key cooperative institution in drought-prone Latur and test whether Mahayuti can maintain local cohesion after one of its own ministers sided with the opposition. A total of 999 voters will elect 19 directors. Thirty candidates are in the fray, while four have already been elected unopposed.
Article Summary: The election to Latur District Central Cooperative Bank on Sunday has emerged as the clearest public sign yet of cracks within Mahayuti. At the centre of the rift is cooperation minister and NCP member Babasaheb Patil, who broke ranks with the alliance and backed the Congress panel. Thirty candidates are in the fray, while four have already been elected unopposed.

A 54-year-old Warkari from Sainik Takali village in Shirol taluka of Kolhapur district died after an unknown vehicle hit him at Bhose Phata on the Sangli-Solapur stretch of the Nagpur-Ratnagiri National Highway in the early hours of Sunday.The deceased was identified as Uttam Babaso Patil. : Farmers from Maval will meet chief minister Devendra Fadnavis in Mumbai on Nov 19 to press for long-pending rehabilitation demands and reiterate their opposition to the Pavana closed pipeline project, which aims to supply water directly from the dam to Pimpri Chinchwad.The chief minister has invited representatives of two groups for the meeting, with five farmers from each delegation expected to attend. One group is seeking rehabilitation for those whose land was acquired for construction of Pavana dam in 1972. The other is opposing Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation’s closed pipeline project, arguing that it would stop the release of water into Pavana river, affecting villages and farmers downstream who depend on it for irrigation.“This will be the first meeting between farmers and chief minister. On Oct 1, the CM assured us over the phone that he would hold a meeting to address our concerns. We then called off our protest, led by Raju Shetti, in Maval,” said Dnyaneshwar Dalvi, president, Pavana Closed Water Pipeline Project Kruti Samiti.Dalvi said former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar had earlier held a meeting with farmers, during which discussions on rehabilitation of project-affected families made some progress, though no final decision was taken.Former Pune guardian minister Girish Bapat had also held discussions with them.Farmers who gave up their land for the dam have been demanding four acres of land for each affected family. During a meeting with Ajit Pawar, it was proposed that two acres could be allotted from unused land acquired for the dam project, while the remaining two acres could be provided elsewhere in the district, depending on availability. However, the proposal has not yet been implemented.The Nov 19 meeting assumes significance as the state govt and civic body are looking to revive the project, which has remained stalled since 2012, when three farmers protesting against it were killed in police firing.Earlier this year, Fadnavis held a meeting with elected representatives from Maval and Pimpri Chinchwad, along with officials from the relevant departments, to discuss the project’s revival. He assured them that farmers would be taken into confidence before any decision was made.The project is considered vital for Pimpri Chinchwad, with civic officials claiming it could save an additional 100 MLD of water that is otherwise lost to evaporation in the open river. They have also argued that the closed pipeline would ensure better water quality by preventing contamination.
Article Summary: Farmers from Maval will meet chief minister Devendra Fadnavis in Mumbai on Nov 19. The high court on Monday orally remarked that police cannot stereotype DJ parties as events where drugs are consumed.The court was considering an appeal filed by the state govt challenging a single bench order that permitted late-night DJ parties at five-star classified hotels and set aside police notices issued to a hotel at Kadavanthra restricting such parties. The police action in the case concerns DJ parties and not the consumption of alcohol or the permitted operating hours of bars, a bench comprising Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji observed.“Policing cannot be based on assumptions and generalisations,” the court said. Distinguishing policing from police raj, the court clarified that policing is not merely about acting after a crime has been committed but also about prevention, as statutorily permitted.The crackdown on drugs and prohibited substances should continue at all times and with such force and vigour as may be absolutely necessary, the bench said, adjourning the appeal to Nov 20.Additional advocate general Mohammed Shah, appearing for the state govt, contended that the police notices issued to the bar hotel at Kadavanthra were not intended to restrict its permitted operating hours but to prevent unrestrained and uncontrolled parties where drugs and other substances were allegedly used openly. However, the hotel management submitted that it took full responsibility for the parties and ensured that every customer was screened for drugs and other prohibited substances.
Article Summary: The high court on Monday orally remarked that police cannot stereotype DJ parties as events where drugs are consumed. The court was considering an appeal filed by the state govt challenging a single bench order that permitted late- night DJ parties at five-star classified hotels.
